reason: The septum should divide the heart into right and left sides, preparing the two routes. It is the only available action.
expectation: I expect a heart with separated chambers, still needing valves and vessel connections.

effect: The septum divided the heart and exposed inlet and outlet valve slots; the reference panel shows why valves are needed.
reaction: The reversing arrows make the purpose of the valves clear.
reason: I'll fit the inlet valves first to address one of the two marked slots.
expectation: I expect the ventricular inlets to gain valves, with the outlets still needing them.

alternatives.reason: The outlet valves are also needed, but either set seems reasonable to fit first.

effect: The inlet valves are fitted, and the squeeze and filling frames show how they direct flow. The outlet valves remain to be fitted.
reaction: The contrasting frames make the inlet valves' role clear.
reason: Fit the outlet valves to complete the remaining valve slot; it is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the ventricular outlets to gain valves that help prevent backward flow.

effect: Both valve sets are fitted; the outlet valves limit blood returning from the arteries between beats.
reaction: The ejection and return arrows clearly distinguish the outlet valves' role.
reason: Add conducting tissue to prepare the heart to pump; it is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the heart to gain electrical pathways that coordinate its contractions, though the details are uncertain.

effect: The conducting tissue gives the heart a timed electrical wave, with atrial contraction followed by ventricular contraction.
reaction: The matching wave and squeeze arrows make the coordination clear.
reason: Connect the pulmonary loop to begin linking the heart to its routes; it is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the heart to connect to the lung vessel loop, while the systemic route and blood may still need connecting.

effect: The pulmonary route now connects the right heart to the lung capillaries and back to the left atrium; the body route remains open.
reaction: The separate open connection makes the next step clear.
reason: Connect the systemic vessels to complete the route toward body tissues; this is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the systemic network to connect to the heart, with blood and possibly the heart's own vessels still to add.

effect: The heart now connects to separate pulmonary and systemic loops; its own vessels and blood still appear to need adding.
reaction: The two-route framework is clear, though this was a predictable connection.
reason: Add the heart’s own blood vessels; it is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect coronary vessels to connect to the heart muscle, with blood still to add.

effect: The heart muscle now has its own coronary supply and venous return, distinct from blood in the chambers.
reaction: The distinction explains why the pump needs its own vessels, though the coronary sinus is not explained.
reason: Add blood to the connected circulation; this is the only available gameplay action.
expectation: I expect blood to enter the pulmonary and systemic routes and complete the circulation goal.

effect: Adding blood completed the circulation goal, showing both routes and the coronary branch together.
reaction: The route arrows bring the separate constructions together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the heart’s own vessels was most worthwhile: it explained why blood in the chambers cannot supply all the thick heart muscle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the systemic network was a predictable, mandatory step; its resulting picture added little explanation beyond showing the two loops.

surprise.text: The separate coronary supply changed my understanding of how the pump itself is fed.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose, though the coronary sinus appeared without an explanation; a brief identification of it would help this audience.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in continuing to see how circulation connects to other body functions, although this chapter offered few meaningful choices beyond valve order.
